idiom_name: role objects plus __getattr__ forwarding (or per-instance bound methods); ABCs for role interfaces
implementation_notes: Python attaches behaviour per instance for free: a method can be bound to one object (types.MethodType) and missing attributes can be forwarded to a role registry with __getattr__, so the classic ComponentRole forwarding class shrinks to a two-line hook while roles stay ordinary objects holding their core. Role interfaces can be declared with abc.ABCMeta and recognized structurally through register/__subclasshook__ (virtual subclasses), so role classes need no common base. Use explicit role classes with dataclasses or __slots__ when roles are persisted, introspected or validated; the dynamic hook then remains only the lookup protocol.
pitfalls: Implement __getattr__, never __getattribute__: the former runs only for missing attributes, the latter intercepts everything and easily recurses.
Core-role reference cycles are collected by CPython's cycle GC but can delay __del__ and finalization; keep one direction weak when lifecycle matters.
Per-instance attributes and injected bound methods do not survive pickling or copying unless implemented, and instances using __slots__ reject injected methods.
